notes.title: Linux Build Updated
notes.content:
I've updated the Linux build to be inline with the newest Windows build. 

It is important to note that - depending on the version of Ubuntu you have - additional dependencies may need to be installed to permit you to play the game. The dependencies are:

libcurl4
libopenal1

You should install these packages on your machine otherwise the games might not run.

Try this in the terminal:

sudo apt update
sudo apt-get install libcurl4
sudo apt-get install libopenal1

notes.title: The Future of 'The Superfluous'
notes.content:
As of about a year ago, I've decided that The Superfluous is a done game. It completes the purpose and fulfilled my vision for the game. Is it perfect? Not at all. Are there things I'd change? Probably. I'll do a full post mortem someday but now it is time to move on. The game will only receive updates if someone finds a bug or someone requests a good quality of life update. The world The Superfluous created though is far from over. I have at least 2 more games I'd like to build in the world 'after the asteroid'.

Some of you might know that a year ago I started creating the sequel to The Superfluous, The Superfluous Sand, and posted at itch.io.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26570085/984d1ee5f22f7aff8532e6830dfb5859d6dfb368.png[/img]

[url=https://voidedpixels.itch.io/superfluous-sand]The Superfluous Sand[/url]

As of right now the Alpha is fairly far along and is free. So check it out if you'd like.

The story continues sometime later after the events of The Superfluous and it takes place on Earth. I've decided to change the format of this game to a top-down survival base building game in the same vein as Rim World but having you control a single person. This was always the plan (the third game will be different too) as it would be hard for me as a solo dev to make the same game over and over again and then justify you buying the same just rehashed. I want to continue to learn and grow as well. I am keeping the art style and humor so it should still look and feel like a Superfluous game. You'll even still have some familiar characters to speak to (E.D.I.E.).

Expect a Kickstarter (like I did for The Superfluous) and a much more polished and complete game. The Superfluous took me about 2 months to make. The Superfluous Sand is going on over a year of development.

Personal life (a flood, an adoption, and 3 hospital stays with our new baby girl) has kept me from keeping in touch with you guys. That is totally on me and I apologize. I hope to keep you guys on STEAM updated with my progress as this development gets closer to release. This was my first big game and I've learned a lot from this whole experience. I've even grown to like a few of you :) Hopefully, I will be able to bring you an even greater game in the near future!

If you want to follow my development more closely click on that link above and check out all the dev-logs and get involved in the community. You'll even see I made a few card games along the way :)

I've decided after several years to drop the price to 99 cents! Pick it up and enjoy it that's all I ask :)

Happy gaming my lovely peeps!

notes.title: Update
notes.content: I double the gem/coin gain from all enemies and mining activities. Hopefully, this is something you wanted and will help lessen the grind. I also added two new buttons on the LEFT menu to disable VSYNC and enable alt timing. Most of you won't need to use these options but are included for those that have high Hz monitors.

notes.title: Mac Build - Reinstall?
notes.content:
I updated the Mac build to hopefully fix some errors some people are experiencing (IE ground disappearing). I've yet to replicate these errors on my machine so it is hard to debug. Thank you to everyone on the forum trying to help me nail down this annoying bug.

YOU MIGHT NEED TO REINSTALL the game to get it to run properly. If it updates and you can run it great but if not do this. [This will not erase any progress you made] In your game list right-click 'The Superfluous' and select uninstall. Then reinstall. Play.

The good thing about this is it should run with less lag on old Macs.

notes.title: Learn more about The Superfluous
notes.content:
[url=http://www.thesuperfluous.com/]The Superfluous Website[/url]

"The Superfluous" [soo-pur-floo-uh s] is cave-diving, sci-fi, rogue-lite, platformer with jet packs and lots of explosions. The game focuses on navigating an asteroid fighting enemies and collecting loot to level up your team of intrepid explorers. The Superfluous has a fun story and features a squad system that allows you to switch your squad members in and out when needed.

Other Features
- Couch co-op: bring a friend along and yell at them for getting your guys killed.
- 4 player local arena mode: take said friend and kill them for fun (in the game of course).
- Rogue Lite: when you die (which you will do) you won't lose all of your progress.
- Story: a fun story about the end of the world, bureaucracy, the military, and sci-fi culture.
- Controller Support

Available on PC, Mac, and Linux (tested on Ubuntu 16.04)

notes.title: Co-Op Revive
notes.content:
I went ahead and added a co-op revive.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26570085/d1bfc20407a7dbc3618d4e52e8d6e1783dcfde38.png[/img]

If a player dies in co-op and the team has ran out of squad mates to switch to, the other player can revive the current player in the body of the last squad mate they controlled. I added this so the two people can continue playing together. The revived player will die if they take any damage, but they can heal with a health pack.

I hope this helps to make co-op a little more fun.
